title: Modifié Fisher Grading échelle pour Subarachnoid hémorragie (SAH)

how_to_use.why:
- Allows timely preventative treatment for vasospasm and DCI to be initiated (vasospasm typically occurs between 4 and 14 days (“vasospasm window”) after the onset of aSAH. ([Fisher 1983](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6682190))
- Vasospasm is common in aSAH and often results in DCI, which occurs in up to 46% of all patients and can cause devastating neurological consequences and/or death. ([Claassen 2001](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11546890))
- The MFS is widely used and well-known in the critical care and neurocritical care communities.
how_to_use.pearls:
- L'échelle de gradation de Fisher modifiée (Modified Fisher Grading Scale, MFS) aide à prédire le risque de vasospasme clinique et d'ischémie cérébrale retardée (DCI) dans l'hémorragie sous-arachnoïdienne anévrismale (aSAH). Elle améliore l'échelle de Fisher originale en intégrant la présence d'une hémorragie intraventriculaire (IVH).
- La MFS est entièrement radiographique et généralement déterminée lors de la présentation initiale.
- Quatre grades MFS de base (1-4) correspondent au risque de vasospasme clinique.
- Les taux de vasospasme pour chaque grade MFS varient selon les études. Le grade MFS ne doit pas être interprété comme une probabilité exacte de développer un vasospasme ou une DCI.
- Ne doit PAS être utilisé comme seul élément de données pour prendre des décisions sur la prise en charge médicale ou les objectifs de soins.
- N'a pas été initialement développée pour prédire la mortalité, mais une revue récente a montré que le grade MFS est associé à la mortalité hospitalière. ([Lantigua 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/26330064))
- De même, la MFS n'a pas été initialement conçue pour prédire le devenir neurologique, mais une analyse rétrospective a montré que les grades MFS sont associés à une probabilité plus élevée de devenir neurologique défavorable. ([Kramer 2008](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/18671630))
- Ne s'applique PAS aux hémorragies sous-arachnoïdiennes dues à un traumatisme, aux malformations artérioveineuses, aux angiomes caverneux, aux fistules artérioveineuses durales, aux thromboses veineuses corticales ou sinusales, aux anévrismes mycotiques, ou aux emboles septiques avec transformation hémorragique.

next_steps.advice:
- Neurological and neurosurgical consultation should be obtained for patients with evidence of any SAH on imaging or lumbar puncture, whether the SAH is likely to be aneurysmal or non-aneurysmal in nature.
- Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) of the head is helpful to determine the presence of a lesion suitable for surgical or endovascular intervention.
- Consider discussing need for cerebrovascular imaging, such as CTA of the head or catheter angiography, with neurological or neurosurgical consultant before ordering.
- Similarly, consider deferring the decision to start medications that have been shown to alter outcomes in aSAH (such as nimodipine and/or aminocaproic acid) to the neurological or neurosurgical consultant.

evidence:
- The MFS is based on the findings of J. Claassen and colleagues from Columbia University Medical Center, who first showed that thick cisternal subarachnoid hemorrhage and IVH in 2 lateral ventricles were both independently associated with DCI in a retrospective multivariate analysis of 276 patients with aSAH. They proposed a scale whose grades accounted for thickness of subarachnoid hemorrhage and bilateral lateral ventricular IVH in 4 different combinations (risks for each grade not shown here). ([Claassen 2001](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11546890))
- Frontera et al. further modified the scale, based on data from a retrospective multi-center cohort of 1,355 patients with aSAH, by replacing bilateral ventricular IVH from Claassen et al.’s previous scale with any IVH as a predictor of symptomatic vasospasm.
- Risks of symptomatic vasospasm ([Frontera 2006](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16823296)):

 - Grade 1 (focal or diffuse, thin SAH, no IVH): 24%
 - Grade 2 (focal or diffuse, thin SAH, with IVH): 33%
 - Grade 3 (focal or diffuse, thick SAH, no IVH): 33%
 - Grade 4 (focal or diffuse, thick, SAH, with IVH):40%
- A retrospective single-center study of 237 patients with aSAH showed a steady increase in the risk of clinical vasospasm, cerebral infarction, and poor neurological outcome with each increase in MFS grade, suggesting that it may also have prognostic value with respect to neurological outcome, in addition to predicting vasospasm. ([Kramer 2008](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/18671630))

 - This same study also determined the risks of vasospasm:

 - Grade 1: 6%
 - Grade 2: 15%
 - Grade 3: 35%
 - Grade 4: 34%
- A single-center retrospective study of factors associated with excellent functional outcome in 373 patients with aSAH found that lower MFS grade was not associated with excellent functional outcome in a multivariate analysis. ([Pegoli 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25495745))
- A retrospective single-center study of 1,200 patients with aSAH showed that higher MFS grade (but not DCI) was associated with a significantly increased odds of in-hospital mortality in a multivariate analysis (OR 1.25, 95%CI 1.0-1.5). ([Lantigua 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/26330064))
more_info:
**Interprétation du score :**

| Grade de Fisher modifié | Risque de vasospasme symptomatique |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | 0% |
| 1 | 6-24% |
| 2 | 15-33% |
| 3 | 33-35% |
| 4 | 34-40% |
